pillar_reactions.evidence: Delivered at length (3-4 sessions/week, 30-45 minutes, strength plus stamina plus a 5-15 minute daily mobility routine). Anthony's only response was 'Yeah, sounds good' and then 'Yeah, of course' to 'do you feel like that is something that you can stick to those three to four workouts a week?'. No questions, no tie-back to his own goals. Worth noting the pillar was pre-sold before it was presented — he had already volunteered 'it sounds logical that the kettlebell, it just makes a little bit more sense about the impact it has on your actual mobility'.

Presented as whole foods, no calorie counting, no chicken-and-rice, plus light intermittent fasting. Anthony answered 'Yeah.' and 'Great.' He had already identified nutrition as his weak point earlier ('I just, I don't have any consistency, I would say'), but he added nothing when it was presented back to him.

Presented as the umbrella: one-to-one with Trevor, onboarding call, app tracking, form video review, Trevor's personal number, the Skool community and a Thursday live workout. Anthony's response to the whole block was 'All right, that's good. Thank you.' and 'Yeah. Great.' Notably he had earlier signalled he did not want indefinite dependence — 'I just want to learn, you know... instead of having to be with us for the rest of eternity' — and the rep pre-empted that with the teach-a-man-to-fish framing, which drew no pushback.

anchors.raw: I'm trying to go on training programs, like not programs, like workout sessions that you can find on YouTube, whatever... I would like to find something a little bit more, like a little bit more assistance, because I'm learning on watching video, like it's, I don't feel like... Like I'm learning anything, you know?
anchors.note: His current solution costs nothing. He is already dissatisfied with it, which is the opening, but nobody quantified the gap between free and $6,000, so the whole distance had to be carried by the pitch.

anchors.raw: There's a couple of guys also that do, you know, kettlebell trainings and everything online.
anchors.note: Stated in answer to 'why kettlebells' — he is aware of a field of online kettlebell providers he has not priced against Primal. Never explored, so it remains live during his week of thinking.

anchors.raw: I've never spent that much money in anything like that, you know, and it would be a big ask because all of my money is in my business right now, so, you know, I'm being very careful
anchors.note: A personal-spend ceiling rather than a competitor number: $6,000 would be his largest ever discretionary purchase, and his liquidity is tied up in a growing business. High nominal business income with low personal liquidity — the anchor is cashflow, not value.

anchors.raw: plenty of people go for a personal trainer in a gym they're okay with being with them for [forever]
anchors.note: Raised by the rep, not the prospect, and immediately rejected — Anthony's whole frame is that he wants to stop needing a coach. Weak support at best; the rep used an anchor his prospect had already declined.

unmet_demand.want: Concrete third-party financing terms he could compare against the internal plan — 'If you can send me the different options by email so I can review it, what would make the most sense.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep could not state the terms: 'we have to check because the, yeah, the interest is always different. I don't know if you would actually get [it]... is it like, is it based in the U.S.?' No provider, rate or term was named on the call.

unmet_demand.want: A written summary of the value and the payment options to review before deciding — 'Just a summary of the things we, of the value that you bring, and I know you mentioned the two options for payment plans.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nothing written appears to exist to send; the offer lives entirely in the verbal pitch, so a self-directed buyer who wants to read before he commits has nothing to read. The rep offered 'I can send you a whole essay' — an improvised document, not an asset.

unmet_demand.want: To be taught the system well enough to run it himself afterwards — 'help me just build a program that I can learn. So once I have it, you know, I can just keep on going.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Partially served: the rep addressed it directly with the teach-a-man-to-fish framing and the graduation picture ('when you go on vacation in a year from now and you're not working with us anymore, you just know how to pick up a kettlebell'). Left here because it is a demand for a finite engagement that the six-month price is not explicitly framed against, and it is the demand most exposed to a cheaper alternative.
